If they are not able to keep the intruder\f + \fr 14.17  \ft Gk \fq it \f* away, they do what they can to help their young by flying in circles around them in the anguish of love, warning them with their own calls.
And why is it necessary to demonstrate sympathy for children by the example of unreasoning animals,
since even bees at the time for making honeycombs defend themselves against intruders and, as though with an iron dart, sting those who approach their hive and defend it even to the death?
But sympathy for her children did not sway the mother of the young men; she was of the same mind as Abraham.
O reason of the children, tyrant over the emotions! O religion, more desirable to the mother than her children!
Two courses were open to this mother, that of religion, and that of preserving her seven sons for a time, as the tyrant had promised.
She loved religion more, the religion that preserves them for eternal life according to God's promise.\f + \fr 15.3  \ft Gk \fq according to God\f*

In what manner might I express the emotions of parents who love their children? We impress upon the character of a small child a wondrous likeness both of mind and of form. Especially is this true of mothers, who because of their birth pangs have a deeper sympathy toward their offspring than do the fathers.

Considering that mothers are the weaker sex and give birth to many, they are more devoted to their children.\f + \fr 15.5  \ft Or \fq For to the degree that mothers are weaker and the more children they bear, the more they are devoted to their children.\f*
The mother of the seven boys, more than any other mother, loved her children. In seven pregnancies she had implanted in herself tender love toward them,
and because of the many pains she suffered with each of them she had sympathy for them;
yet because of the fear of God she disdained the temporary safety of her children.
Not only so, but also because of the nobility of her sons and their ready obedience to the law, she felt a greater tenderness toward them.
For they were righteous and self-controlled and brave and magnanimous, and loved their brothers and their mother, so that they obeyed her even to death in keeping the ordinances.
Nevertheless, though so many factors influenced the mother to suffer with them out of love for her children, in the case of none of them were the various tortures strong enough to pervert her reason.
But each child separately and all of them together the mother urged on to death for religion's sake.
O sacred nature and affection of parental love, yearning of parents toward offspring, nurture and indomitable suffering by mothers!
This mother, who saw them tortured and burned one by one, because of religion did not change her attitude.

She watched the flesh of her children being consumed by fire, their toes and fingers scattered\f + \fr 15.15  \ft Or \fq quivering \f* on the ground, and the flesh of the head to the chin exposed like masks.
O mother, tried now by more bitter pains than even the birth pangs you suffered for them!
O woman, who alone gave birth to such complete devotion!
When the firstborn breathed his last, it did not turn you aside, nor when the second in torments looked at you piteously nor when the third expired;
nor did you weep when you looked at the eyes of each one in his tortures gazing boldly at the same agonies, and saw in their nostrils the signs of the approach of death.

When you saw the flesh of children burned upon the flesh of other children, severed hands upon hands, scalped heads upon heads, and corpses fallen on other corpses, and when you saw the place filled with many spectators of the torturings, you did not shed tears.
Neither the melodies of sirens nor the songs of swans attract the attention of their hearers as did the voices of the children in torture calling to their mother.
How great and how many torments the mother then suffered as her sons were tortured on the wheel and with the hot irons!
But devout reason, giving her heart a man's courage in the very midst of her emotions, strengthened her to disregard, for the time, her parental love.

Although she witnessed the destruction of seven children and the ingenious and various rackings, this noble mother disregarded all these\f + \fr 15.24  \ft Other ancient authorities read \fq having bidden them farewell, surrendered them\f* because of faith in God.
For as in the council chamber of her own soul she saw mighty advocates—nature, family, parental love, and the rackings of her children—
this mother held two ballots, one bearing death and the other deliverance for her children.
She did not approve the deliverance that would preserve the seven sons for a short time,
but as the daughter of God-fearing Abraham she remembered his fortitude.
O mother of the nation, vindicator of the law and champion of religion, who carried away the prize of the contest in your heart!
O more noble than males in steadfastness, and more courageous than men in endurance!
Just as Noah's ark, carrying the world in the universal flood, stoutly endured the waves,

so you, O guardian of the law, overwhelmed from every side by the flood of your emotions and the violent winds, the torture of your sons, endured nobly and withstood the wintry storms that assail religion.
If, then, a woman, advanced in years and mother of seven sons, endured seeing her children tortured to death, it must be admitted that devout reason is sovereign over the emotions.
Thus I have demonstrated not only that men have ruled over the emotions, but also that a woman has despised the fiercest tortures.

The lions surrounding Daniel were not so savage, nor was the raging fiery furnace of Mishael so intensely hot, as was her innate parental love, inflamed as she saw her seven sons tortured in such varied ways.
But the mother quenched so many and such great emotions by devout reason.
Consider this also: If this woman, though a mother, had been fainthearted, she would have mourned over them and perhaps spoken as follows:
“O how wretched am I and many times unhappy! After bearing seven children, I am now the mother of none!
O seven childbirths all in vain, seven profitless pregnancies, fruitless nurturings and wretched nursings!
In vain, my sons, I endured many birth pangs for you, and the more grievous anxieties of your upbringing.

Alas for my children, some unmarried, others married and without offspring.\f + \fr 16.9  \ft Gk \fq without benefit\f* I shall not see your children or have the happiness of being called grandmother.
Alas, I who had so many and beautiful children am a widow and alone, with many sorrows.\f + \fr 16.10  \ft Or \fq much to be pitied\f*
And when I die, I shall have none of my sons to bury me.”
Yet that holy and God-fearing mother did not wail with such a lament for any of them, nor did she dissuade any of them from dying, nor did she grieve as they were dying.
On the contrary, as though having a mind like adamant and giving rebirth for immortality to the whole number of her sons, she implored them and urged them on to death for the sake of religion.
O mother, soldier of God in the cause of religion, elder and woman! By steadfastness you have conquered even a tyrant, and in word and deed you have proved more powerful than a man.
For when you and your sons were arrested together, you stood and watched Eleazar being tortured, and said to your sons in the Hebrew language,
“My sons, noble is the contest to which you are called to bear witness for the nation. Fight zealously for our ancestral law.
For it would be shameful if, while an aged man endures such agonies for the sake of religion, you young men were to be terrified by tortures.
Remember that it is through God that you have had a share in the world and have enjoyed life,
and therefore you ought to endure any suffering for the sake of God.

For his sake also our father Abraham was zealous to sacrifice his son Isaac, the ancestor of our nation; and when Isaac saw his father's hand wielding a knife\f + \fr 16.20  \ft Gk \fq sword \f* and descending upon him, he did not cower.
Daniel the righteous was thrown to the lions, and Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael were hurled into the fiery furnace and endured it for the sake of God.
You too must have the same faith in God and not be grieved.
It is unreasonable for people who have religious knowledge not to withstand pain.”
By these words the mother of the seven encouraged and persuaded each of her sons to die rather than violate God's commandment.
They knew also that those who die for the sake of God live to God, as do Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the patriarchs.
Some of the guards said that when she also was about to be seized and put to death she threw herself into the flames so that no one might touch her body.
O mother, who with your seven sons nullified the violence of the tyrant, frustrated his evil designs, and showed the courage of your faith!
Nobly set like a roof on the pillars of your sons, you held firm and unswerving against the earthquake of the tortures.
Take courage, therefore, O holy-minded mother, maintaining firm an enduring hope in God.

The moon in heaven, with the stars, does not stand so august as you, who, after lighting the way of your star-like seven sons to piety, stand in honor before God and are firmly set in heaven with them.

For your children were true descendants of father Abraham.\f + \fr 17.6  \ft Gk \fq For your childbearing was from Abraham the father\ft ; other ancient authorities read \fq For . . . Abraham the servant\f*   
\s1 The Effect of the Martyrdoms

If it were possible for us to paint the history of your religion as an artist might, would not those who first beheld it have shuddered as they saw the mother of the seven children enduring their varied tortures to death for the sake of religion?
Indeed it would be proper to inscribe on their tomb these words as a reminder to the people of our nation:\f + \fr 17.8  \ft Or \fq as a memorial to the heroes of our people\f*
“Here lie buried an aged priest and an aged woman and seven sons, because of the violence of the tyrant who wished to destroy the way of life of the Hebrews.
They vindicated their nation, looking to God and enduring torture even to death.”
Truly the contest in which they were engaged was divine,
for on that day virtue gave the awards and tested them for their endurance. The prize was immortality in endless life.
Eleazar was the first contestant, the mother of the seven sons entered the competition, and the brothers contended.
The tyrant was the antagonist, and the world and the human race were the spectators.
Reverence for God was victor and gave the crown to its own athletes.
Who did not admire the athletes of the divine\f + \fr 17.16  \ft Other ancient authorities read \fq true \f* legislation? Who were not amazed?
The tyrant himself and all his council marveled at their\f + \fr 17.17  \ft Other ancient authorities add \fq virtue and\f* endurance,
because of which they now stand before the divine throne and live the life of eternal blessedness.
For Moses says, “All who are consecrated are under your hands.”

These, then, who have been consecrated for the sake of God,\f + \fr 17.20  \ft Other ancient authorities lack \fq for the sake of God\f* are honored, not only with this honor, but also by the fact that because of them our enemies did not rule over our nation,
the tyrant was punished, and the homeland purified—they having become, as it were, a ransom for the sin of our nation.
And through the blood of those devout ones and their death as an atoning sacrifice, divine Providence preserved Israel that previously had been mistreated.
For the tyrant Antiochus, when he saw the courage of their virtue and their endurance under the tortures, proclaimed them to his soldiers as an example for their own endurance,
and this made them brave and courageous for infantry battle and siege, and he ravaged and conquered all his enemies.
O Israelite children, offspring of the seed of Abraham, obey this law and exercise piety in every way,
knowing that devout reason is master of all emotions, not only of sufferings from within, but also of those from without.
Therefore those who gave over their bodies in suffering for the sake of religion were not only admired by mortals, but also were deemed worthy to share in a divine inheritance.
Because of them the nation gained peace, and by reviving observance of the law in the homeland they ravaged the enemy.

The tyrant Antiochus was both punished on earth and is being chastised after his death. Since in no way whatever was he able to compel the Israelites to become pagans and to abandon their ancestral customs, he left Jerusalem and marched against the Persians.   
\s1 The Mother's Address to Her Children
The mother of seven sons expressed also these principles to her children:
“I was a pure virgin and did not go outside my father's house; but I guarded the rib from which woman was made.\f + \fr 18.7  \ft Gk \fq the rib that was built\f*
No seducer corrupted me on a desert plain, nor did the destroyer, the deceitful serpent, defile the purity of my virginity.

In the time of my maturity I remained with my husband, and when these sons had grown up their father died. A happy man was he, who lived out his life with good children, and did not have the grief of bereavement.
While he was still with you, he taught you the law and the prophets.
He read to you about Abel slain by Cain, and Isaac who was offered as a burnt offering, and about Joseph in prison.
He told you of the zeal of Phinehas, and he taught you about Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael in the fire.
He praised Daniel in the den of the lions and blessed him.
He reminded you of the scripture of Isaiah, which says, ‘Even though you go through the fire, the flame shall not consume you.’
He sang to you songs of the psalmist David, who said, ‘Many are the afflictions of the righteous.’
He recounted to you Solomon's proverb, ‘There is a tree of life for those who do his will.’
He confirmed the query of Ezekiel, ‘Shall these dry bones live?’
For he did not forget to teach you the song that Moses taught, which says,
‘I kill and I make alive: this is your life and the length of your days.’”

O bitter was that day—and yet not bitter—when that bitter tyrant of the Greeks quenched fire with fire in his cruel caldrons, and in his burning rage brought those seven sons of the daughter of Abraham to the catapult and back again to more\f + \fr 18.20  \ft Other ancient authorities read \fq to all his\f* tortures,
pierced the pupils of their eyes and cut out their tongues, and put them to death with various tortures.
For these crimes divine justice pursued and will pursue the accursed tyrant.

But the sons of Abraham with their victorious mother are gathered together into the chorus of the fathers, and have received pure and immortal\f + \fr 18.23  \ft Other ancient authorities read \fq victorious \f* souls from God,
to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

headers.ip: Mark long tah Khrih he Pathen capa la om tih Pathen neh hlang kah tueihyoeih la om (1:1). Tedae thaomnah neh hlang taengah bibi a bi. (Cael 10:38; Rom 15:8,9). Bibi khuiah a len koek neh a then koek tah hlang tloe ham bibi he ni (9:35; 10:42-45). Mark long he Jesuh kah a thuituennah lakah a bibinah kawng he a yet a tueng sak. Jesuh kah thuinuetnah ol voei (4) bueng a tueng sak tih kopoekrhai sainah tah voei (18) tueng. Tedae Mathai dongah (14) Luka dongah (15) ni a tueng.

\wj Te long te anih taengah, ‘Na mana te ha pawk coeng. Te dongah na pa loh vaito puetsuet te a ngawn tih anih te sading la a doe,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Te dongah kosi a hong tih kun ham ngaih pawh. Tedae a napa tah cet tih anih te a hloep.\wj*
\wj Tedae a napa te a doo tih, ‘Kum, he yet na taengah sal ka bi tih na olpaek ka poe moenih he. Tedae kai ham tah ka paya neh uum hamla maae pataeng nan paek moenih.\wj*
\wj Tedae hlanghalh rhoek neh na khosaknah aka yoop na capa tah ha pawk vaengah, vaito puetsuet te anih ham na ngawn pah,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Tedae a napa loh amah te, ‘Camoe aw, nang tah kai taengah rhawp na om tih, kai koe boeih he nang hut coeng ni.\wj*
\wj Tedae uum vaengah khaw omngaih ham a kuek ta. Na mana tah aka duek la om coeng dae ha hing koep, poci coeng dae koep ha phoe,’ a ti,”\wj* a ti nah.
A hnukbang rhoek te khaw, \wj “Hlang pakhat tah kuirhang la om tih hnokhoem a khueh. Te long te a khuehtawn a haeh pah dongah amah a khotoh nah.\wj*
\wj Te dongah anih te a khue tih, ‘Nang kawng ka yaak he me tlam lae? Na hnokhoemnah dongkah olka te thuung laeh, na khoom ham na coeng voel moenih,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Te vaengah hnokhoem amah te, ‘Balae ka saii lah eh? Ka boeipa loh hnokhoemnah he kai lamloh a lat coeng, diklai daeng ham khaw ka noeng pawh, bih ham khaw ka yak,\wj*
\wj Ka saii ham te ka ming coeng. Te daengah ni hnokhoemnah lamkah ka puen uh vaengah a im khuila kai n'doe uh eh,’ a ti.\wj*
\wj Te dongah, a boeipa kah purhong rhoek te rhip a khue tih, lamhma taengah, ‘Ka boeipa taengah meyet na ba?’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Te long te, ‘Situi um yakhat,’ a ti nah. Te vaengah anih te, ‘Na cabu na doe vaengah ngol pahoi lamtah sawmnga mah daek,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Pakhat te khaw, ‘Nang tah meyet na ba,’ a ti nah. Te long te, ‘Cang phueih yakhat,’ a ti nah. Anih te, ‘Cabu na doe vaengah sawmrhet la daek,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj A thai a lai neh a saii dongah boethae kah hnokhoem te boeipa loh a koeh. Ta kumhal kah ca rhoek he amah cadil khuiah tah vangnah kah a ca rhoek lakah cueih uh.\wj*
\wj Te dongah kai loh nangmih taengah ka thui, Boethae laikhuehtawn te khaw na paya la khueh uh. Te daengah ni dungyan dap khuila na khum vaengah n'doe uh eh.\wj*
\wj A yit dongah uepom la aka om tah a len dongah khaw uepom la om tih, a yit dongah aka halang tah a len dongah khaw halang.\wj*
\wj Halang, laikhuehtawn neh uepom la na om uh pawt bal atah unim nangmih rhep aka tangnah te?\wj*
\wj Te dongah na hlanglang tih uepom la na om pawt atah na koe te u long nangmih m'paek eh.\wj*

\x - \xo 16.13 \xt Mat 6. 24\x*\wj Imkhut pakhat loh boei panit kah sal a bi thai moenih, pakhat te a toeng vetih pakhat te a lungnah ni, pakhat te a talong vetih pakhat te a hnoel ni. Pathen neh laikhuehtawn kah sal na bi rhenten thai moenih,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Ram Kah A Phu
Te te naivoei la aka om Pharisee rhoek loh boeih a yaak uh vaengah amah te a nueih thil uh.
Te dongah amih te, \wj “Nangmih loh hlang hmaiah aka tang la na om uh. Tedae Pathen loh nangmih thinko te a ming. Hlang soah aka sang te Pathen hmaiah tueilaehnah la om.\wj*
\x - \xo 16.16 \xt Mat 11. 12,13\x*\wj Olkhueng neh tonghma rhoek loh Johan hil, te lamkah loh Pathen kah ram tah ana phong coeng tih a khuila la boeih ana ael uh.\wj*
\x - \xo 16.17 \xt Mat 5. 18\x*\wj Olkhueng te a dek pakhat a rhul lakah vaan neh diklai a khum te a phoeng la om pueng.\wj*

\x - \xo 16.18 \xt Mat 5. 32; 1Ko 7. 10,11\x*\wj A yuu te a tueih tih a tloe aka lo boeih tah samphaih coeng. Te phoeiah va aka ma aka yunah te khaw samphaih.\wj*   
\s1 Kuirhang neh Lazarus
\wj “Hlang pakhat tah kuirhang la om. Te dongah daidi, hnithen neh khuk uh tih hnin takuem thayoei tuipan la a uum.\wj*
\wj Te vaengah khodaeng pakhat, a ming ah Lazarus tah buhlut neh a vongka ah a yalh pah.\wj*
\wj Te dongah kuirhang caboei lamkah aka bo nen te bunghah khaw a nai. Tedae ui rhoek long pataeng ha pawk uh vaengah a buhlut te a laeh pa uh.\wj*
\wj Tedae khodaeng te a duek vaengah puencawn rhoek loh Abraham rhang dongla a khuen. Te phoeiah kuirhang te khaw duek tih a up uh.\wj*
\wj Tedae saelkhui ah a mik a hoh tih nganboh neh kho a sak vaengah tah Abraham neh a rhang dongkah Lazarus te a hla lamkah a hm uh.\wj*

\wj Te dongah a pang neh, ‘A pa Abraham, kai he n'rhen lamtah Lazarus te han tueih mai. A kutdawn kah a hmoicue te tui dongah naek saeh lamtah ka lai he sul sak saeh, hmaitak khuiah mat n'yuek coeng he,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Tedae Abraham loh, ‘Camoe, na hingnah dongkah na hnothen na dang te poek. Te vaengah Lazarus tah yoethae bangla om. Tedae anih a mong vaengah he nang tah patang loh n'yuek coeng.\wj*

\wj He rhoek boeih khuiah khaw kaimih neh nangmih laklo kah longhoi tah muep n'lak coeng. Te dongah nangmih taengla hlaikan dingdoeng aka ngaih long khaw coeng pawh, kaimih taengla hlaikan dingdoeng ham khaw coeng pawh,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Te phoeiah, ‘A pa namah ni kan hloep. Te dongah anih te a pa im la tueih mai.\wj*
\wj Manuca panga ka khueh dongah amih te uen mai saeh. Te daengah ni amih khaw hekah nganboh hmuen la ha pawk uh pawt eh,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Tedae Abraham loh, ‘Moses neh tonghma te a khueh uh ta, amih taengah hnatun uh saeh,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Tedae te long te, ‘Moenih, a pa Abraham, aka duek tangtae pakhat loh amih te paan koinih yut uh ni,’ a ti nah.”\wj*
\wj “Tedae anih te, ‘Moses neh tonghma rhoek kah olthui te a hnatun uh pawt atah, duek khui lamkah khat khat thoo cakhaw ngaitang mahpawh,’ a ti nah,”\wj* a ti.
Te phoeiah a hnukbang rhoek te, \wj “Thangkui te a thoeng pawt ham om tloel coeng. Tedae anunae anih lamloh aka thoeng sak aih.\wj*
\wj He camoe rhoek khuikah pakhat a khah ham lakah tah a rhawn ah lungto phaklung a oi tih tuili la voei koinih anih ham hoeikhang lah.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.3 \xt Mat 18. 15\x*\wj Namamih te ngaithuen uh, na manuca loh a tholh atah amah te toel, a yut atah anih te hlah laeh.\wj*

\wj Hnin at neh nang soah voei rhih tholh coeng dae namah taengla voei rhih ha bal tih, ‘Ka yut,’ a ti coeng atah anih te hlah laeh,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Tangnah neh Pongthoh Nah
Caeltueih rhoek loh Boeipa taengah, “Kaimih ham tangnah han thap lah,” a ti uh.
Tedae Boeipa loh, \wj “Tangnah he mukang mu tet na khueh uh koinih, hekah thaihae kung he, ‘Phong uh lamtah tuili ah phung,\wj*’ \wj na ti uh mai cakhaw nangmih kah te a ngai ni.\wj*
\wj Nangmih khuiah sal aka khueh te tah lai a thol pah tih boiva a dawn pah. Lohma lamkah a paipaek vaengah anih te u long, ‘Ha kun lamtah cawt ngol dae,’ a ti na eh?\wj*
\wj Anih te, ‘Mebang khaw tawn lamtah ka ca eh, te phoeiah cihnin vaep lamtah ka caak ka ok vaengah kai taengah thotat, te phoeiah ni na caak na ok eh,’ ti na mahpawt nim?\wj*
\wj A uen te a saii dongah sal soah lungvatnah khueh mapawt nim?\wj*

\wj Nangmih khaw, nangmih ng'uen te boeih na saii uh tangloeng dae, ‘Kaimih tah sal hlangkhue hlangvaih rhoek ni, saii ham a kuek te ni n'saii,’ ti uh mai,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Hmaibae Hlangrha
Jerusalem la a caeh a om vaengah Jesuh tah Samaria neh Galilee laklo longah cet.
Te vaengah vangca pakhat la a kun hatah hmaibae hlang parha loh Jesuh te a doe uh tih amamih tah soei pai uh.
Te phoeiah a ol a huel uh tih, “Boeipa Jesuh kaimih n'rhen lah,” a ti uh.

\x - \xo 17.14 \xt Tho 14. 1-32\x*Amih te a hmuh vaengah, \wj “Cet uh lamtah namamih te khosoih rhoek taengah tueng uh,”\wj* a ti nah.  
 Tedae a caeh uh li vaengah mah amih te boeih cim uh.
Tedae amih khuikah pakhat long tah a hoeih te a hmuh vaengah bal tih ol ue la Pathen te a thangpom.
Te phoeiah anih tah Samaria dae ni a kho kung ah maelhmai a buluk thil tih Jesuh te a uem.
Te dongah Jesuh loh a doo tih, \wj “Parha la a cim uh moenih a? Pako rhoek ta melae?\wj*
\wj Anih kholong hlang pawt atah Pathen te thangpomnah paek ham aka bal hmu uh boel saeh a?”\wj* a ti nah.

Te phoeiah anih te, \wj “Thoo, cet laeh, namah kah tangnah loh namah ng'khang coeng,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Ram Ha Pai
Pathen kah ram ha pawk vaengkah te Pharisee rhoek loh a dawt dongah amih te a doo tih, \wj “Pathen kah ram tah hmuhnah neh ha pawk moenih.\wj*
\wj ‘He la he, ke la ke,’ ti uh mahpawh. Pathen kah ram tah namamih khuiah ni a om te,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te phoeiah hnukbang rhoek te, \wj “Khohnin ha pawk vaengah hlang capa kah khohnin te hnin at hmuh ham na hue uh suidae na hmuh uh mahpawh.\wj*
\wj Nangmih taengah, ‘Ke la ke, he la he,’ a ti uh akhaw cet uh boeh, hnuktlak uh boeh.\wj*
\wj Khophaa loh phaa tih vaan hmui pakhat lamkah loh vaan hmui pakhat la sae ni. Hlang capa tah amah tue vaengah ha om tangloeng bitni.\wj*
\wj Tedae lamhma la muep a patang ham neh tahae cadil loh a hnawt ham khaw a kuek.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.26 \xt Sue 6. 5-8\x*\wj Noah tue vaengkah a om vanbangla, hlang capa kah a tue vaengah khaw om van ni.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.27 \xt Sue 7. 6-24\x*\wj Noah lawng khuila a kun khohnin duela yuloh rhaihlan neh a caak a ok uh. Te dongah tuilii ha pawk vaengah boeih poci.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.28 \xt Sue 18. 20—19. 25\x*\wj Lot kah khohnin vaengah khaw amah boeiloeih la om uh tih a caak uh‍, a ok uh‍, a lai uh‍, a yoih uh‍, a tawn uh‍, a sak uh‍.\wj*
\wj Tedae Sodom lamkah loh Lot a caeh khohnin ah, vaan lamkah hmai neh kat a tlan pah tih boeih poci.\wj*
\wj Hlang capa a pumphoe tue vaengah amah boeiloeih la om ni.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.31 \xt Mat 24. 17,18; Mrk 13. 15,16\x*\wj Te khohnin vaengah imphu ah aka om tah, im khuikah a hno te loh hamla suntla boel saeh. Lohma kah long khaw a hnuk la mael van boel saeh.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.32 \xt Sue 19. 26\x*\wj Lot yuu te poek uh.\wj*
\x - \xo 17.33 \xt Mat 10. 39; 16. 25; Mrk 8. 35; Luk 9. 24; Jhn 12. 25\x*\wj A hinglu te kutloh ham aka toem long tah poci ni, tedae aka hlong long tah tekah a hing thil ni.\wj*
\wj Nangmih taengah ka thui, tekah khoyin ah panit loh thingkong pakhat dongah om rhoi cakhaw, pakhat te a khuen vetih pakhat te a hlun ni.\wj*
\wj Amah nawn ah sum aka kuelh panit om ni. Pakhat te a khuen vetih, pakhat a hlun ni,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te dongah amah te a doo uh tih, “Melae Boeipa,” a ti na uh.
Tedae amih te, \wj “Rhok te tah langta loh pahoi a bo van ni,”\wj* a ti nah.
Thangthui yoeyah ham neh thathae pawt ham a kuek soah amih te nuettahnah neh a voek tih,
\wj “Kho pakhat ah laitloekkung pakhat om tih Pathen taengah birhih pawt tih hlang taengah a yahnah om pawh.\wj*
\wj Te vaengah kho khuiah aka om nuhmai loh anih te a paan tih, ‘Ka kocaelh hmaiah kai n'tang sak,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Tedae te khohnin ham ngaih pawh. Te phoeiah amah te, ‘Pathen taengah ka birhih pawt tih hlang te ka yahnah mai ngawn pawh.\wj*
\wj Te akhaw he nuhmai he kamah thakthaenah la n'toeh dongah anih ka tang sak eh. Te daengah ni a bawtnah la pawk vetih kai n'ngae pawt eh,’ a ti,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te phoeiah Boeipa loh, \wj “Laitloekkung loh a boethae kah a cal te ya uh.\wj*
\wj A taengah khoyin khothaih aka pang, a coelh hlang kah kutthungnah te Pathen loh a saii mueh moenih. Te dongah amih taengah a thinsen a?\wj*

\wj Nangmih taengah ka thui te, amih kah kutthungnah te thamaa la a saii ni ta. Tedae hlang capa ha pawk vaengah tangnah he diklai hmanah a hmuh venim?”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Pharisee neh Mangmucoi Kah Thangthuinah
A dueng la om ham amah neh amah pangtung tih a tloe aka hnaelcoe hlangvang rhoek te khaw hekah nuettahnah neh,
\wj “Hlang panit tah thangthui ham bawkim la cet rhoi. Pakhat tah Pharisee tih pakhat te mangmu aka coi ni.\wj*
\wj Pharisee tah amah la pai tih, ‘Hlang tloe kutveet aka khueh, halang rhoek, samphaih rhoek, neh he kah mangmucoi bangla ka om pawt dongah Pathen nang he kan uem,\wj*
\wj Sabbath te hnavoei ka yaeh, ka kaelh boeih te parha pakhat la vawpvawp ka paek,’ tila thangthui.\wj*
\wj Tedae mangmucoi tah soei pai tih mik pataeng vaan la a dai ngaih pawh. A lungkoe te a tum tih, ‘Pathen aw, ka tholh he han dawth lah,’ a ti.\wj*

\x - \xo 18.14 \xt Mat 23. 12; Luk 14. 11\x*\wj Nangmih taengah ka thui, anih he pakhat lakah aka tang ngai la a im te a paan. Te dongah amah neh amah aka pomsang boeih tah a tlarhoel sak ni. Tedae amah neh amah aka yalh tah a pomsang ni,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Camoe a Uem
Te vaengah cahni rhoek te taek van saeh tila amah taengla a bawnhlak uh. Tedae hnukbang rhoek loh a hmuh vaengah amih te a tlung uh.
Tedae Jesuh loh amih a khue tih, \wj “Camoe rhoek te kamah taengla ha pawk ham han hlah uh, amih te kang uh boeh. Amih ham ni Pathen kah ram a om.\wj*

\wj Nangmih taengah rhep ka thui, Pathen kah ram te camoe bangla aka doe pawt long tah a khuiah kun loengloeng mahpawh,”\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 Khoboei Cadong
Jesuh te boei pakhat loh a dawt tih, “Saya then, mebang ka saii nen lae dungyan hingnah ka pang eh?” a ti nah.
Te dongah anih te Jesuh loh, \wj “Balae tih kai he then na ti? Pathen amah bueng pawt atah aka then a om moenih.\wj*

\x - \xo 18.20 \xt Sng 20. 14; Olr 5. 18; \xt Sng 20. 13; Olr 5. 17; \xt Sng 20. 15; Olr 5. 19; \xt Sng 20. 16; Olr 5. 20; \xt Sng 20. 12; Olr 5. 16\x*\wj Olpaek rhoek te na ming coeng, samphaih boeh, hlang ngawn boeh, huen boeh, laithae boeh, na pa neh na nu te hinyah,”\wj* a ti nah.
Tedae te long te, “Te rhoek te ka camoe lamkah loh boeih ka tuem coeng,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.

A yaak vaengah Jesuh loh anih te, \wj “Pakhat na vawt pueng. Na khueh sarhui te boeih yoi lamtah khodaeng rhoek ham tael pah. Te daengah ni vaan ah khohrhang na khueh eh. Te phoeiah kai taengah pahoi ha bang,”\wj* a ti nah.

Tedae anih te kuirhang la muep a om dongah te ol te ngang a yaak vaengah sut om.   
\s1 Khuehtawn neh Pathen Ram
Ngang a yaak te Jesuh loh a hmuh vaengah, \wj “Tangka aka khueh rhoek loh Pathen kah ram khuila a kun ham tah bahoeng kuel mai.\wj*
\wj Kuirhang te Pathen ram khuiah a kun lakah phamet khui ah kalauk a kun te a phoeng la om,”\wj* a ti nah.
Aka ya rhoek loh, “Te koinih unim aka daem thai ve?” a ti uh.
Tedae Jesuh loh, \wj “Hlang loh a tloel nah te Pathen taengah tah yoeikoek la om mai,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te vaengah Peter loh, “Amah kah imlo aka toeng kaimih long tah namah kam vai uh he,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.
Te dongah Jesuh loh amih te, \wj “Nangmih taengah rhep ka thui, Pathen kah ram ham im khaw, yuu khaw, manuca khaw, manu napa khaw, a ca khaw aka toeng te a om moenih.\wj*

\wj Anih tah tahae tue vaengah a pawklaih neh kumhal ah dungyan hingnah aka thoeng te dang mueh pawt suidae?\wj* a ti nah.   
\s1 A Dueknah Te A Thui Bal
Hlainit te a khuen tih amih taengah, \wj “Jerusalem la cet uh sih ne, tonghma rhoek loh a daek hlang capa kawng te boeih soep pawn ni.\wj*
\wj Namtom rhoek taengah a voeih vetih a tamdaeng ni, a neet ni, a timthoih ni,\wj*
\wj Anih te a boh uh vetih a ngawn uh ni, tedae a thum hnin ah koep thoo ni,”\wj* a ti nah.

Tedae amih loh te te a hmuhming uh moenih. Hekah oltak long he amih taeng lamloh a thuh uh pueng dongah a thui te yakming uh pawh.   
\s1 Mikdael Loh Kho A Hmuh
Jerikho te a pha tom vaengah mikdael pakhat loh long taengah ngol tih a bih.
Hlangping kah a pah te a yaak vaengah, “Balae aka om he,” a ti.
Te vaengah Nazareth Jesuh a pah te a taengla a puen pa uh.
Te dongah pang tih, “David Capa, Jesuh, kai n'rhen lah,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.
Te vaengah aka lamhma rhoek loh anih te kamkhuem sak ham a ho uh. Tedae anih te muep lat pang tih, “David capa kai ng'rhen lah,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.
Te dongah Jesuh tah pai tih, anih te amah taengla mawt hamla ol a paek. A yoei uh vaengah Jesuh loh mikdael amah te a dawt.

\wj “Nang ham na ngaih te balae kan saii eh,”\wj* a ti nah.  
 Te vaengah mikdael loh, “Boeipa, hmuh ham,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.
Jesuh loh anih te, \wj “Tueng saeh, namah kah tangnah loh nang n'khang,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te vaengah pahoi a hmuh dongah Jesuh hnuk a vai doeah Pathen te a thangpom. Pilnam boeih long khaw a hmuh vaengah Pathen te thangthennah a paek.
Jerikho te a kun thil tih a hil.
Te vaengah hlang pakhat, a ming ah Zakkhaeus la a khue te lawt om. Anih tah mangmu boei neh kuirhang la om.
Anih long khaw Jesuh te hmuh hamla a toem. Tedae a pumrho he merheh la a om dongah hlangping te aep thai pawh.
Tedae a khum ham te a om coeng dongah a hmai la a khal tih amah hmuh ham thaibah dongla yoeng.
Tekah hmuen la a pha vaengah Jesuh tah oeloe tih anih te, \wj “Zakkhaeus, a loe la rhum, tihnin ah nang im ah ka naeh ham a kuek,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te dongah suntla tok tih Jesuh a doe te omngaih coeng.
Boeih a hmuh uh vaengah cai uh tih, “Hlang tholh taengah pah hamla kun,” a ti uh.

A pai neh Zakkhaeus loh Boeipa taengah, “Boeipa, Ka khuehtawn he rhakthuem he khodaeng rhoek ka paek. Hlang khat khat kah hno khat khat ni ka rhawt pah bal atah rhaepli la ka thuung coeng he,” \w a\w* \w ti\w* \w nah\w*.
Te dongah anih te Jesuh loh, \wj “Anih tah Abraham capa la a om van dongah tihnin ah tah khangnah loh he imkhui la pai coeng.\wj*

\x - \xo 19.10 \xt Mat 18. 11\x*\wj Hlang Capa ha pawk he aka poci te toem ham neh khang ham rhoe pai ni,”\wj* a ti.   
\s1 Tangka Nuettahnah
Jerusalem a pha tom vaengah a yaak neh Pathen kah ram a tueng hamla cai tomlael coeng tila a poek dongah nuettahnah pakhat te a thap tih a thui.
Te dongah, \wj “Tongpa hlangtang pakhat tah, a ram loh ham kho hla la cet tih ha voei hamla cai.\wj*
\wj Te dongah a sal hlangrha te a khue tih mina lungrha te amih taengah a paek. Te phoeiah amih te, ‘Amah ka pawk hil thenpom uh,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Tedae a pilnam rhoek loh anih te a hmuhuet uh. Te dongah amah hnukah laipai tloep a tueih uh tih, ‘Kaimih soah a manghai ham he ka ngaih uh moenih,\wj*’ \wj a ti na uh.\wj*
\wj Ram te a loh tih amah ha mael vaengah tah tangka a paek a sal rhoek te amah taengla a khue tih metla a thenpom uh khaw ming hamla a dawt.\wj*
\wj Te vaengah aka pawk lamhma loh, ‘Boeipa, nang kah mina pakhat te mina parha ka kum thil,’ a ti nah.\wj*
\wj Te vaengah anih te, ‘Then, sal then a yit dongah uepom la na om tih, kho parha soah saithainah aka khueh la om laeh,’ a ti nah.\wj*

Te phoeiah amih te, \wj “Nangmih taengah ka om vaengah nangmih ham ka thui ka ol tah he ni. Moses kah olkhueng neh tonghma rhoek, tingtoeng dongah khaw kai kawng a daek te boeih a soep ham a kuek ta,”\wj* a ti nah.
Te daengah cacim hmuhming ham te a lungbuei puk uh.
Te dongah amih te, \wj “Khrih a patang ham neh a thum hnin ah duek lamkah a thoh ham khaw,\wj*
\wj Jerusalem lamkah loh tong uh lamtah namtom boeih taengah tholh khodawkngainah ham yutnah te amah ming neh hoe ham a daek tangloeng coeng.\wj*
\wj Nangmih tah he rhoek kah laipai rhoek ni.\wj*

\s1 Jesuh Vaan La Luei
\x - \xo 24.50 \xt Clt 1. 9-11\x*Amih te Bethany duela voelh a khuen phoeiah a kut a phuel tih amih te yoethen a paek.
Amih yoethen a paek nen tah amih taeng lamloh khoe uh tih vaan la a khuen.
Te vaengah amih loh amah te a bawk uh tih Jerusalem ah omngaihnah neh muep bal uh.
Te phoeiah bawkim khuiah om taitu uh tih Pathen te a uem uh.

headers.im: Jesuh Khrih he u laeh? He oldawtnah he Johan loh olthangthen cabu a tong vaengah hlatnah a khueh. Khrihca a tongcuek kah rhoek loh laa a sak uh vaengah Jesuh Khrih he a ming phoei uh pawt tih (Oltak) lam ni a thui. A ming a phoei uh moenih. Te oltak dongah Pathen loh a cungkuem a suen. A cungkuem te hingnah a paek. (Aboel 1.3,4). Johan Olthangthen loh Jesuh Khrih tah “Diklai tholhnah aka khuen Pathen tuca” (1.29). Philip loh “Moses loh a kawng a thui te” (1.45) Jesuh ni ti a ming. “Pathen capa Israel manghai” (1.49) a ti.
headers.ip: Johan long tah Pathen capa Messiah dongah tangnah khueh uh rhep a ti. (20.31).

headers.ip: Tangnah kawng aka pung sak khungdaeng tih namtom taengah olthang then aka thui koek Paul kawng he khaw a thui bal. Te vaengah Khopuei a len koek la aka om Rom khopuei ah Paul loh olthangthen a thui (28.16—31). Paul loh olthangthen a thui te u long khaw a paa sak thai moenih.

headers.im: Korin Khrihca hlang boel taengla Paul tlek a caeh thai pawt vaengah tah Paul te a noih uh. Te kawng te amih ham koep a thuicaih pah. Te vaengah Paul loh a lungbuei te a then ben la a hoi. (1.23). A hnukbang rhoek long khaw a uen bangla khosak sak te a ngaihnah om. A ka tholh khaw khodawk ngai tih pilnam te hloep ham a ngaih bal. (2.5—11).
headers.ip: Pathen tah moeihoeih Pathen la a om dongah Jerusalem neh Judea kah kah hlang rhoek ham bomnah a paek uh. (8.1—-9.15). Paul tah olkhueh thai dongkah Pathen tueihyoeih la om (3.1—17). Amah te bahoeng patang dae Pathen taengla pilnam mawt ham tlungmu. (4.1—-6.13; 10.1—-12.10). He cabu he AD 57 tluk vaengah a tael.

headers.id: GAL GALATIANS Matupi Chin Standard Bible
headers.im: He kah ca he Asia Minor kah Galati hlang boel rhoek ham a tael pah. Paul amah he caeltueih tang la om tih, a olthang khaw oltak ni tite a cimphan la a thui. (1.1-10).
headers.ip: Paul he caeltueih tak tak ni. Anih he namtom taengah missionary la Boeipa loh a tueih tih Jerusalem ah tah caeltueih taktak la a pom. (1.18—-2.10). Peter he namtom rhoek kah caak ok kawng dongah kapyik kapyok la a om dongah Paul loh rhaprhap a toel (2.1—18). Tangnah he hi khangnah daemnah longpuei la a om. Abraham kah tangnah kawng a tip la Paul rhep rhep a thui. Galati capat he AD 57vaengah a tael.

headers.id: PHP - Matupi Chin Standard Bible With Strong's Number
headers.im: Paul loh hekah ca he thongim ah a tael ( 1.7) tih Philipi hlangboel taengah a pat. Philipi Khrihca rhoek nen khaw thangthuinah dongah pat mueh la pha uh thae (1.5; 4.10-19). Thongim lamloh a loeih atah olthangthen thui ham a ngaiuep (3.17-19). Tedae Paul loh amah kah a dueknah ham kawng khaw a ming. (1.21; 2.17; 3.10).
headers.ip: Philipi hlangboel khuiah tuituknah bet aka om tah daemnah aka om thai pawh olkhueng rhuem bangla khosak a ngoe aka ti a om dongah. Olkhueng rhuem la aka cet rhoek tah Paul long tah a tloh la a voek tih ui a ti nah (3.2-11). Paul he thongim ah om dae Khrih a khueh dongah omngaihnah soep a khueh tih Khrihca hlang boel rhoek khaw khueh uh van a ti nah. Hekah capat he tah

headers.im: Kolosa he khotlak Asia Minor kah Phrygia peng ah om tih Ephesa neh Rom khopuei kah longpuei ah om. Paul amah he Kolossa kho ah om pawh. Tedae amih kah tangnah a cak te a yaak (1.3-7; 2.6,7). Amih kah olthang te thongim ah a om vaengah (Philemon 23) Epaphras (1.7; 4.12,13) loh a thui pah tih hekah capat he pahoi a tael (1.14; 4.3,10,18).
headers.ip: Kolossa hlangboel kah Khrihca rhoek he namtom (Gentiles) (1.27) hlang yet ngai. Te dongah amih te kholong kah bawknah a tloe tloe loh muep a poek (2.16-23). Pumsa neh a tloe kah mueihla bawknah he Pathen pumpaeknah bangla a poek uh tholh. Te dongah Paul loh Khrih he vaan ah Pathen neh om coeng lunglai boeih khaw a uk tila a thui (3.1). Te dongah bawknah dongah he Khrih ni a kungpuei la khueh ham a thui. Kolosa capat he AD 60 tluk vaengah a tael.

headers.im: Paul loh Thessalonika hlang boel a pai sak (2.13,14) vaengah he amah loh bi mat a bi (2.9). Thessalonika he Greek tlangpuei ah olpuei khopuei la om. Kutsaii aka bawk he muep om dae Khrihca la boeih kun uh (1.9). Tedae amih te Boeipa dongah uepom la om uh tih amih kah olthang te paeng tom la yilhcet (1.8). Hekah capat he Olkhueh Thai khuiah lamhma cuek a tael la om coi ni.
headers.ip: Hlangboel khuiah a lolhnah om. A ngen long tah Boeipa ha rhum pawn ni tila a poek tholh dongah bi aka bi mueh khaw om uh (4.11,12). A ngen bal tah Khrih a rhum hlan ah aka duek a huiko ham mawntangnah a khueh uh. Te dongah Paul loh Khrih a rhumnah kawng te cimphan la a thuicaih pah (4.13-15). Amih ham te tahae tue metlam kho n'sak eh ti khaw a thui pah (5.1-11). Hekah capat he AD 50-54 tluk vaengah a tael.

headers.im: Thessalonika hlangboel rhoek he tangnah neh lungnah dongah a rhoeng uh he ni Paul loh Pathen a uemnah lamhmacuek (chapter 1.3). Amih te ngaihmangnah muep om dae Pathen kah datatnah pawt tih noemcaihnah ni tila amih taengah a thui (1.4,5).
headers.ip: Paul loh yalpo bingak he a ngaih moenih (3.6-10), ol aka ngai pawt te a then la rhalrhing uh a ti nah.

headers.im: Timothy tah a manu Jews hoel tih a napa he Greek hoel la om. A camoe lamloh thangthai tih Pathen a ming coeng (1.5). Paul neh cet rhoi tih bi a bi rhoi (Romans 16.21; 1Kor 16.10; Philipi 2.19). Tangnah dongah tah Paul loh a capa la a khueh (1.2). Timothy he Paul kah uepom bibipuei la a khueh te capat dongah voei nga a tueng sak.
headers.ip: Hekah capat dongah he Paul loh Timothy amah ham khaw ca a tael pah. Te phoeiah Khrihca hlangboel kah khosaknah neh mawtkung (3.1-7), bibikung(3.8-13), neh a hamca (5.17-20) tueknah kawng a thui. Hekah capat he AD 64 tluk vaengah a tael.

headers.im: Lamhma kah lakah khaw a pabae dongah he Paul loh Timothy amah ham oluennah muep a khueh. Timothy he a oingaih a ca la om tih thangthuinah dongah rhawp a khueh (chapter 1.2,3). Timothy loh muep a ueh dongah Khrih kah rhalkap then la om (2.1,3). Timothy he a manu neh a numca loh mueihla ben ah a rhoengnah hamla a camoe lamloh a tukkil coeng.
headers.ip: Paul loh a dueknah tue khaw laplap a ming, tedae uepomnah thapang khaw anih hamla om coeng (4.6-8), dongah Timothy olrho a pat (2.11,12a).

headers.im: Paul loh Titus he Asia Minor neh Greek ah a om vaengkah bibipuei la puetpuet a thui (2 Kor 2.13; 7.6,13; 8.6,16,23; 12.18; Galati 2.3). Paul loh Titu taengah Crete kah bibikung rhoek te tuek a ti nah.
headers.ip: Crete kah hlangcom hlangcae boeih te Paul loh ol a uen. Hingnah longpuei thai he tah Pathen loh Jesuh Khrih han tueih dongah ni. Pathen loh hlang hing a khang, a silh tih dungyan hingah, ngaiuepnah a paek. (3.4,5). Titus capat he AD 65 vaengah a tael.

headers.im: Philemon tah kuirhang hlangcong la la om tih sal khaw muep a khueh. A im khaw len tih Khrihca hlangboel a pumnah la a hnonah. Paul loh Kolosa capat dongah Onesimus ming a tueng sak poek vaengah Philemon he Kolosa kho ka mai coi ni tila poeknah om (Kolosa 4.9,17).
headers.ip: Rom khokah lunglai ah tah tahae kah catael aka then koek catael pakhat la om a ti. Hekah capat dongah Paul neh Philemon he payan thintlo rhep la om a ti. Tahae kah capat he Rom ram lunglai ah hlang tom loh tae a ngaih. Hekah capat he AD 65 vaengah a tael.

headers.im: Hebrew capa aka taelkung he Paul, Apollos, Silas, Barnabas, amih khui kah khatkhat loh tael mai coini a ti uh. Cataelkung he u lae ti m'ming mai pawt cakhaw Pathen Mueihla Cim loh hil a paek Pathen ol ni tila ming he ni olpuei ngai. Khat ben ah Hebrew capat a tael vaengah Khrihca rhoek haemtaeknah muep a om dongah cataelkung ming phoe pawt mai coini.
headers.ip: He kah capat he Rom caem loh Jerusalem a pan tih bawkim boeih a phae, hlang tamta la boeih a khuennah AD 70 tluk vaengah a tael.
